zones.title: Rust Belt
zones.text: Dead industry, corroded catwalks, railway yards, and foul pools. Metal-feeding fungi find a foothold here. After dark, Rust Rats emerge; sometimes their red eyes are all you can see.

additionalImage.alt: A Rust Rat at night, its red eyes glowing among the industrial ruins

zones.title: Hollow Wood
zones.text: An old, dark forest in a twilight of its own, with a moon too large.

additionalImage.alt: An owl with bright eyes perched among the dark red trees at night

zones.title: Glass Desert
zones.text: A vast land of sand, mineral crust, and ground fused into glass. Shade is scarce; its landscapes and landmarks are still being tuned.

zones.title: Mountains
zones.text: Ranges of bare rock, pines below, snow on the tops that never melts.

zones.title: Sporelands
zones.text: Where the network breaks the surface.

zones.title: Autumn Fields
zones.text: Old open country gone to tan grass, goldenrod and asters, the trees turned orange, red and gold.

places.title: The works
places.text: Factory halls, warehouses, ironworks, tank farms, and catwalks over the streets: a different scale of abandoned world.

places.title: A stop at the edge of the desert
places.text: A damaged canopy, abandoned pumps, and a kiosk beside the road. Four old gas mascots appear on signs and billboards: Flame, the smiling flame; Droppy, the fuel droplet; Tiger; and Dilly, the armadillo. These scraps of roadside branding give each stop its own character.

places.title: Museum & library
places.text: Some buildings hold traces of what people knew and valued. A skeleton in a museum, a book in a library: there is more to find than raw materials.

places.title: Hollow Manor
places.text: A walled park deep in a Hollow Wood: a stream all the way round with stone bridges over it, an iron fence on a stone wall, a drive between lanterns that still burn, a graveyard, a glasshouse.

places.title: Drive-in after dark
places.text: An outdoor screen, abandoned cars, and a lot returning to grass. A place built for gathering now waits quietly beneath the stars.

image.alt: An abandoned drive-in movie theater with parked cars beneath the stars

mascots.alt: Flame, Droppy, Tiger, and Dilly on four GAS 24H billboards

cards.title: Rusted Pipe
cards.text: Plumbing that carried water once. Hollow, heavy, useful.

cards.title: Circuit Board
cards.text: Pulled from old electronics. Whoever can read these can rebuild things.

cards.title: Scrap Hatchet
cards.text: A blade cut from sheet metal, bolted to a haft. Bites into wood.

cards.title: Scrap Pickaxe
cards.text: A spike of sheet steel on a haft. Slow, but ore gives to it where a pry bar just skids.

cards.title: Wrench
cards.text: Hold it to see the pipes: what joins what, where the water flows, what each pump is doing. X on a pipe shuts or opens its valve.

cards.title: Magnifier
cards.text: A lens in a brass rim. Carry it and you notice more: everything teaches you a little more.

cards.title: Book
cards.text: Swollen with damp. Most pages are still readable.

cards.title: Research Notes
cards.text: Your own notes on a subject.

cards.title: Rare Book: A Natural History of the Fungi
cards.text: A great folio of hand-coloured plates, every gill drawn. Read it (hold it, LT): a great deal of Mycology, more if you're studying it.

image.alt: Rare Book: A Natural History of the Fungi inventory icon

cards.title: Canned Food
cards.text: Dented, label faded. The date stamp is unreadable, which might be for the best.

cards.title: Mushroom Soup
cards.text: Mushrooms simmered thin with an inkcap for colour. Warm all the way down.

cards.title: Roasted Puffball
cards.text: Crisp outside, soft and smoky within.

cards.title: Puffball
cards.text: Firm and white inside. Squeeze an old one and it breathes out a cloud of spores.

cards.title: Sand Truffle
cards.text: A knobbly lump dug from the damp under a dry wash. Dense, earthy and rich: the desert's one real meal.

cards.title: Teal Button Mushroom
cards.text: Teal caps that grow thickest where the network is strongest.

cards.title: Rust Rat
cards.text: Out at night in the Rust Belt. Look for the red eyes among the ruined industry.

image.alt: A Rust Rat at night, its red eyes glowing among the industrial ruins

cards.title: Dune Hopper
cards.text: A nocturnal desert creature that hops across the sand and retreats to its burrow.

image.alt: Dune Hopper in the desert at night

cards.title: Glassback Beetle
cards.text: A daytime creature of the glass fields. Its glassy back catches the sun; its behavior is still experimental.

image.alt: Glassback Beetle on the glass fields

cards.title: Owl
cards.text: A nighttime resident of Hollow Wood, watching from the trees.

image.alt: An owl with bright eyes perched among the dark red trees at night

systems.title: Scavenge what remains
systems.text: Search the abandoned world for useful things. A found object can become equipment, material, or the beginning of a new idea.

systems.title: Learn through discovery
systems.text: Holding ingredients brings recipes to mind. Books preserve research, while working at stations opens new possibilities.

systems.title: Work with your hands
systems.text: Craft tools and useful objects, build shelter, and furnish a place of your own. The world can be broken down and rebuilt.

image.alt: Crafting tables, tools, and storage in a warmly lit workshop

systems.title: Read the land
systems.text: Food safety, cold, warmth, and heat give places their own pressures. Exploring means noticing what the environment asks of you.

systems.title: Growth in an inherited world
systems.text: Mycelium spreads across the ground. Buildings arrive with different degrees of ruin and growth; their stories are written into what remains.

image.alt: Vines returning to an industrial catwalk

future.title: Weather
future.text: Rain, storms, and changing weather are planned; they are not playable yet.

future.title: Combat & encounters
future.text: Combat, weapons, and a wider range of creature encounters remain planned work.

future.title: Ritual & enchantment
future.text: Ritual magick and enchantment are planned beyond the mushroom brews currently being explored.

future.title: A deeper fungal network
future.text: Strain affinity and fungal transport through Root Lines are concepts. Their shape may change, and they may never be built.

future.title: A world with other people
future.text: Repopulation and strain-aligned allies are concepts, rather than existing NPC systems.

updates.title: The desert takes shape
updates.text: Recent work built out the Glass Desert: glass-covered ground, a distinctive sky, heat shimmer, and scattered roadside landmarks. The image shows the developing landscape, whose balance is still experimental.

updates.title: Small lives on the glass
updates.text: The Dune Hopper brings movement to the desert night; the Glassback Beetle adds a daytime resident. Recent work focused on their appearance and simple behaviors.

image.alt: The new Glassback Beetle on the glass fields

updates.title: Roadside identity
updates.text: Four gas mascots give the signs and billboards a consistent identity along their roads. This asset preview shows Flame, Droppy, Tiger, and Dilly as they appear on the game’s billboards.

image.alt: Flame, Droppy, Tiger, and Dilly on four GAS 24H billboards

updates.title: Green against the rust
updates.text: The Rust Belt pass added industry, hazards, wildlife, and visual weathering. Catwalks and returning vegetation make the works feel like a place with a past.

image.alt: Vegetation beneath a catwalk in the works
